2- In the verse (هذا نزلهم يوم الدين) there is the device of tahakkum (sarcasm), which has also passed: He called Hell and the kinds of torment and varieties of horrors in it "nuzul" (hospitality) in sarcasm at them, since nuzul is what is prepared for the guest to honour him — as in the words of the Exalted (فبشّرهم بعذاب أليم) — and like the saying of Abū al-Shaʿrāʾ al-Ḍabbī:
وكنّا إذا الجبار بالجيش ضافنا ... جعلنا القنا والمرهفات له نزلا
(Whenever a tyrant came to us as a guest with his army, we made the spears and the keen blades his hospitality.)
I.e. when the tyrant came down upon us with his army as a guest comes down. In it there is sarcasm at him, since he came to make war; so he likened him to one who came seeking kindness, and reinforced (rashshaḥa) that simile by making the spears and the keen, sharpened swords his nuzul, which is the food prepared for the guest.

dervis-irab:57-74.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُمْنُونَ): "amnā yumnī" and "manā yamnī": to emit semen (al-maniyy) into the womb, i.e. the sperm-drop (nuṭfa). Ibn al-Sammāk read "tamnūn" with fatḥa on the tāʾ. The origin is from al-many, which is measuring out (taqdīr). The poet said:
لا تأمنّ وإن أمسيت في حرم ... حتى تلاقي ما يمني لك الماني
(Do not feel secure, even if you find yourself in a sanctuary, until you meet what the Measurer has measured out for you.)
From it comes al-maniyya (death), because it is measured out and comes according to a measure. In al-Mukhtār: "manā, of the pattern ramā, and also amnā."
(قَدَّرْنا): with the doubled and the single [dāl]. [The poet] said:
ومفرهة عنس قدرت لساقها ... فخرت كما تتايع الريح بالقفل
(And many a strong she-camel, mother of fine young — I measured [my blow] for her shank, and she fell, as the wind tosses dry branches about.)
The meaning is: I measured my blow for her shank, struck her, and she fell. Similar in meaning is:
وإن تعتذر بالمحلّ من ذي ضروعها ... على الضيف يجرح في عراقيبها نصلي
(And if she excuses herself from the guest by the drought of her udders, my blade wounds her hamstrings.)
(حُطاماً): al-ḥuṭām is dry, broken stalks of no use as food or nourishment; the root meaning of al-ḥaṭm is breaking. Al-ḥuṭam is the one who drives [the camels] violently, crushing them against one another. [The poet] said:
قد لفّها الليل بسواق حطم ... ليس براعي إبل ولا غنم
ولا بجزار على ظهر وضم
(The night has wrapped them up with a rough, crushing driver — no herder of camels or sheep, nor a butcher at the chopping-block.)
(تَفَكَّهُونَ): al-tafakkuh originally means partaking of various kinds of fruit (fawākih) to eat. Al-fukāha is jesting; from it is the ḥadīth of Zayd: "He was among the most jesting of people with his family." "Rajul fakih": good-humoured. It has been borrowed here for moving from one topic of talk to another. It is also said that its meaning is "you regret", its literal sense being "you cast jest away from yourselves", and jest is cast away only through grief; so it is of the type of taḥarraja and taʾaththama [i.e. tafaʿʿala of privation]. It is also said that (تفكهون) means you wonder; it is said you blame one another; and it is said you lament. All of that is explaining by what is entailed (al-tafsīr bi-l-lāzim).
(لَمُغْرَمُونَ): plural of mughram; the mughram is the one whose wealth has gone without compensation. The root meaning of this group is clinging, and al-gharām is the clinging punishment. Al-Aʿshā said:
إن يعاقب يكن غراما وإن يع ... ط جزيلا فإنه لا يبالي
(If he punishes, it is a lasting torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care [how much].)
(تُورُونَ): al-īrāʾ is making fire appear by striking. One says "awrā yūrī", and "warīyat bika zinādī", i.e. my affair has been lit up through you. One says "qadaḥa fa-awrā" when the fire appears; when it does not produce fire one says "qadaḥa fa-akbā". In al-Miṣbāḥ: "warā al-zandu yarī wariyan, of the pattern waʿā; in a dialect, wariya yarī with kasra on both; and awrā with the alif — that is when it brings out its fire." In al-Mukhtār: "awrāhu ghayruhu: someone else brought out its fire." In the dictionaries: you extract fire from al-zinād, plural of zand. The zand is the stick with which fire is struck, the upper one; the zanda is the lower one, which has a hole in it and is the female. When the two come together they are called zandān, and the plural is zinād. The Arabs strike fire with two sticks, rubbing one against the other.
(الْمُزْنِ): clouds; plural of muzna. In al-Qāmūs: "al-muzn, with ḍamma, is clouds, or the white of them, or the ones bearing water; the piece is a muzna."
(أُجاجاً): in al-Mukhtār: "māʾ ujāj: bitter water, intensely salty. Ajja al-māʾu yaʾujju ujūjan, with ḍamma."
(لِلْمُقْوِينَ): for travellers, i.e. We made it something that travellers benefit from. They were singled out for mention because their benefit from it is greater than that of residents. Quṭrub said: "al-muqwī is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād): the poor man is called muqwī because he is empty of wealth, and the rich man is called muqwī because of his power (quwwa) to obtain what he wants." It is also said that al-muqwī is the one who alights in al-qawāʾ, the land where there is no one; "aqwat al-dār": the abode became empty of its people. Al-Nābigha said:
أقوى وأقفر من نعم وغيّرها ... هوج الرياح بهابي الترب موار
(It has become empty and deserted of Nuʿm, and the reckless winds have changed it with swirling fine dust.)
ʿAntara said:
حييت من طلل تقادم عهده ... أقوى وأقفر بعد أم الهيثم
(Greetings to you, O ruin whose time has grown long; it has become empty and deserted after Umm al-Haytham.)

* I'rab:
(نَحْنُ خَلَقْناكُمْ فَلَوْلا تُصَدِّقُونَ): (نحن) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (خلقناكم) the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (تصدقون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent).
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ): the hamza is for the disapproving interrogative; the fāʾ is conjunctive; (رأيتم) is a past verb and its agent, and its meaning is "tell me"; (ما) is a relative noun meaning "alladhī" (that which), the first object of (رأيتم); and the clause (تمنون) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخالِقُونَ): the interrogative clause is in the place of the second object of (رأيتم). (أنتم) is a subject and the clause (تخلقونه) its predicate. (أنتم) may also be parsed as the agent of an implied verb, i.e. "do you create it?"; when the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it, the pronoun became detached. This is of the category of ishtighāl (preoccupation), and perhaps, in terms of the rules, it is more sound because of the interrogative particle. (أم) is a conjunction; it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), because a clause follows it, and the disconnected one is construed as "bal" (rather) plus the interrogative hamza. So the speech contains two questions: the first, "Do you create it?", whose answer is no; and the second, taken from (أم), i.e. "Rather, are We the creators?", whose answer is yes. (أم) may also be connected (muttaṣila), in which case it is correlative (muʿādila). This view is supported by the fact that the speech amounts to "which of the two things is the case?", and the clause after it is interpreted as a single word. (نحن) is a subject and (الخالقون) a predicate.
(نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ): (نحن) is a subject and the clause (قدرنا) its predicate; (قدرنا) is a verb and its agent; the adverb is attached to (قدرنا); (الموت) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. We made it obligatory and decreed it for you. The wāw is conjunctive or parenthetical; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (ما), and (نحن) its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (مسبوقين) is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the predicate of (ما).
(عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ أَمْثالَكُمْ وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ): (على) is a preposition, and (أن نبدل) is in the interpretation of a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the genitive by (على); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مسبوقين), i.e. no one can outstrip Us in Our replacing your likes. They may also be attached to (قدّرنا بينكم), i.e. We have decreed death among you on [the basis] that We replace [you] — i.e. some people die and other people succeed them — in which case the clause (وما نحن بمسبوقين) is parenthetical. (ننشئكم) is conjoined to (نبدل); (فيما) is attached to (ننشئكم), and the clause (لا تعلمون) is the ṣila, i.e. We bring you into being in forms you do not know, of debased animals that wallow in filth, like apes and swine.
(وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (علمتم) is a verb and its agent; (النشأة) is a direct object and (الأولى) a naʿt (adjective). (فلولا): the fāʾ is conjunctive, (لولا) a particle of urging, and (تذكرون) an imperfect verb and its agent.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded, so refresh your memory of it.
(لَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ): (لو) is conditional; (نشاء) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); the lām occurs in the answer of (لو); (جعلناه) is a verb, its agent and a direct object; (حطاما) is the second object of (جعل); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ظلتم) is an incomplete past verb; its origin is "ẓaliltum" with kasra on the lām, the middle radical having been dropped for lightness; the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause (تفكهون) its predicate; (تفكهون) is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped.
(إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ): inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (مغرمون) its predicate. The clause of (إنّ), its noun and its predicate is the speech quoted by an omitted verb of saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "so you would remain lamenting, saying" — or "you would say" — "(إنّا لمغرمون)", i.e. we are made to bear the loss of what we spent, or we are ruined by the ruin of our provision.
(بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ): (بل) is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction; (نحن) is a subject and (محرومون) a predicate; the clause is conjoined to the one before it.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْماءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ، أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded; (الذي) is an adjective of (الماء), the clause (تشربون) is the ṣila, and the referent pronoun is omitted.
(لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ): its i'rab has preceded. The secret of omitting the lām in this verse and mentioning it in the first verse will come in the Rhetoric section.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَها أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِؤُنَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded.
(نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتاعاً لِلْمُقْوِينَ): (نحن) is a subject and the clause (جعلناها) its predicate; (تذكرة) is the second object; (متاعا) is conjoined to (تذكرة); (للمقوين) is attached to (متاعا) or is an adjective of it.
(فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (implying an unstated condition), i.e. if you have come to know these benefits and dazzling favours, then glorify. (سبّح) is an imperative verb and its agent is "anta" (you); (باسم) is attached to (سبّح) or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. seeking blessing. It is also said that (اسم) is inserted (muqḥam). (العظيم) is an adjective of (ربك).

* Rhetoric:
1- In the aforementioned verses there is the device of ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām (exhaustive division), which has been mentioned before in this book: it consists of the speaker covering all the divisions of the meaning he is dealing with, so that he leaves nothing of it out. He turned from the word of deprivation and withholding to a word that is its consequent (ridf) and follows it, namely the word "jaʿl" (making), when He said (أفرأيتم ما تحرثون أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما). Likewise the word of reckoning [the favour] of water came, where He said (لو نشاء جعلناه أجاجا), with the word "jaʿl" when mentioning deprivation and what has its meaning; while giving came with the word "zarʿ" (sowing) regarding tillage, and with the word "inzāl" (sending down) regarding water. If it is said: why did He emphasise the verb with the lām in His words about the crop (لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما), and not emphasise it about the water, where He said (لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً)? I say: because the crop — its growth, and its drying after freshness until it becomes broken stalks — might be imagined to be the doing of the farmers; that is why He, glory be to Him, said (أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون). Or it might be imagined that its fertility comes from watering, and its drying from the heat of the sun and lack of watering, or the repeated passing of whirlwinds. So He, glory be to Him, informed that He is in reality the doer of all that, and that He is able, if He willed, to make it broken stalks in the state of its growth and the time of its youth and freshness. Since this false impression was possible, eloquence required emphasising the verb of making in it and attributing it to its true Sower and Originator, in order to remove this impression. And since sending down water from the sky is impossible [for creatures], such that no possibility enters of anyone imagining that anyone of all creation is able to do it, there was no need to emphasise the verb in making it bitter; for no one could imagine that anyone sends down water from the sky bitter — nor sweet, which is easier and simpler than the first.
Al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this matter is as follows: "If you say: why was the lām brought into the answer of (لو) in His words (لجعلناه حطاما) and removed from it here? I say: since (لو) enters upon two clauses, the second of which is dependent on the first as the requital is dependent on the condition, and it is not purely conditional like (إن), nor does it govern as it does — the conditional meaning has only pervaded it incidentally, inasmuch as it conveys, regarding the contents of its two clauses, that the second was precluded because the first was precluded — it needed, in its answer, something set up as a sign of this dependency; so this lām was added to be a sign of that. If it is omitted after it has become a well-known sign in its place, that is because when a thing is known and its place is well known, and it has become familiar and customary, one does not mind dropping it from the wording, relying on the hearer's knowledge. Do you not see what is related of Ruʾba, that he used to say 'khayrin' to whoever said to him 'How are you this morning?' — he dropped the preposition because everyone knew its place, and its omission and its presence were alike since the matter was well known. And sufficient for you is the saying of Aws:
حتى إذا الكلّاب قال لها ... كاليوم مطلوبا ولا طلبا"
(Until, when the hound-master said to her: [never have I seen] the like of today for a quarry, nor for a pursuit.)
I say: in the verse of Aws ibn Ḥajar — or of al-Namir ibn Tawlab — there is an omission without which it is not sound, i.e. "he said to her: I have not seen the like of today for a quarry". The pronoun is for the hunting bitch, and al-kallāb is the trainer of the dogs, or the hunter; i.e. the quarry and the pursuit on this day are not like them on another day, but greater. Then al-Zamakhsharī continues: "It may also be said that this lām undoubtedly conveys the meaning of emphasis, so it was brought into the verse about food rather than the verse about drink, to indicate that the matter of food takes precedence over the matter of drink, and that the threat of losing it is more severe and harder, since drink is needed only as a consequence of food. Do you not see that you give your guest to drink only after you have fed him? Were you to reverse it, you would fall under the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ:
إذا سقيت ضيوف الناس محضا ... سقوا أضيافهم شبما زلالا
(When people's guests are given pure milk to drink, they give their guests cold, limpid water to drink.)
One of the Arabs was given a drink and said: 'I drink only on top of a thamīla.' That is why the verse about food was put before the verse about drink." Al-thamīla is pure milk. [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Zamakhsharī's point concerns drinking only after food, and lexicons commonly gloss thamīla as what remains of food in the stomach.]
We return to the verse of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ and say: it is from an ode in which he praised Saʿd al-Dawla Abū al-Faḍāʾil. He was faulted because he praised [them] for giving guests water before mentioning food. Al-makhḍ is milk whose butter has been removed, so it has the meaning of mamkhūḍ (churned); it is also narrated "maḥḍan" with the undotted ḥāʾ, i.e. pure, sweet or sour. Al-shabim is cold, and al-zulāl is sweet [water]. [Translator's note: the verse as quoted above has «محضا» with ḥāʾ, while the explanation treats «مخض» with khāʾ as the primary reading.]
Moreover, since the scholars of rhetoric have given the context (maqām) a role in indicating what is meant, we say that the meaning of the verse is: when people hasten milk to their guests and content themselves with it instead of hastening food, they [the praised ones] hasten food, because of their preparedness for guests; so [the guests] need to drink water, and they give them water to drink before others have fed their guests. So their giving water conveys, with the help of the context, that food was hastened before it, because water customarily follows it; so there is no fault in it.
2- In these verses there is also the device of tashīm (anticipation), which is that the earlier part of the speech indicates what comes later, or the reverse. So in His words (أفرأيتم ما تحرثون) up to His words (أفرأيتم النار التي تورون), the beginnings of these verses require that their endings [Translator's note: the source sentence is defective here, «تقتضي أوائل هذه الآيات أن أواخرها»; evidently «تقتضي أوائل هذه الآيات أواخرها» (the beginnings require the endings)] — a verbal and semantic requirement — just as the words in them harmonise with their neighbouring meanings, the fitting with the fitting and the suitable with the suitable; because the mention of tillage suits the mention of sowing, and the reckoning [of the favour] that He, glory be to Him, did not make it broken stalks suits their being able to enjoy it. On this verse the arrangement of its sister [verses] is to be measured.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: there is no turning it back and no repelling it. «الكاذبة» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «العاقبة» (outcome) and «العافية» (well-being).
He said: Abū Tharwān said to me in his speech: «إن بنى نمير ليس لحدهم مكذوبة» (the Banū Numayr — there is no belying their edge), meaning: belying. Then He said: ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعةٌ﴾ as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), that is: the Event on that day will be lowering one people into the Fire and raising another people into Paradise. Had a reader read «خافضةً رافعةً» (accusative), meaning: when it happens, lowering some people and raising others, (it would be possible); but it is ugly, because the Arabs do not say «إذا أتيتى زائراً» (when you come to me visiting) until they say: «إذا أتيتنى فأتنى زائراً» (when you come to me, come to me visiting) or «ائتنى زائراً». But it is good in al-Wāqiʿa, because before the accusative there is a verse on which it is good to pause, so the implied (verb) becomes good in what begins anew.
«[Translator's note: «أتيتى» is as printed, evidently for «أتيتنى».]»

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلأَرْضُ رَجّاً﴾.
When it is shaken until every building on the face of the earth collapses.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسّاً﴾.
They become like flour; and that is His saying: ﴿وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ﴾. I heard the Arabs recite:
لا تَخْبِزا خَبْزا وبُسّا بَسّا * مَلْسا بذَوْدا لحلَسِّ مَلْسا
(Do not bake bread, but mix (the meal) quickly, and drive the camels on swiftly.)
والحُمّسِ أيضا
And «البسيسة» among them is flour, or barley-meal (sawīq) that is moistened and taken as provision.
«[Translator's note: the second half-verse and the words «والحمس أيضا» are garbled in the printed text; the gloss renders the sense of the commonly cited verse «لا تخبزا خبزا وبسا بسا * ولا تطيلا بمناخ حبسا».]»

farraa:7-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجاً ثَلاَثَةً ﴾; then He explained them, saying: ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾.
He made His Prophet wonder at them, saying: what are the companions of the right? What kind of people are they? They are the companions of the right hand. ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ مَآ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾: He made him wonder at them too; they are the companions of the left hand. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلسَّابِقُونَ﴾. This is the third class. If you wish, you make «السابقين» nominative by the second «السابقين» (i.e. as mubtadaʾ and khabar); they are the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn), and everyone who was first (to believe) in one of the prophets is among these. If you make one of them nominative by the other, it is like your saying «الأول السابق» (the first is the foremost). And if you wish, you make the second an emphasis of the first, and it is made nominative by His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ﴾.
«موضونة» means woven. The Arabs only called the she-camel's girth «وضين» because it is woven. I have heard one of the Arabs say: «فإذا الآجر موضون بعضه على بعض» (and the bricks were laid closely one upon another), meaning: fitted together. [Al-Farrāʾ said: «الوضين» is the girth.]

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ﴾.
It is said that they are of one age and do not change. The Arabs say of a man who has grown old without his hair turning grey: «إنه لمخلّد»; and when his teeth have not gone with old age, it is also said: «إنه لمخلّد». It is also said: «مخلّدون» means wearing earrings; and it is said: wearing bracelets.

farraa:18-18.t:
[191/ا] His saying: ﴿بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ﴾.
«الكوب» is (a vessel) that has neither a spout (lit. ear) nor a handle; and «الأباريق» are those with spouts and handles.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا﴾: from the wine; ﴿وَلاَ يُنزِفُونَ﴾: that is, their minds will not go.
It is said of a man when he is drunk: «قد نُزِف عقله» (his mind has been drained); and when his blood has gone and he has fainted or died, it is said: «منزوف».
Whoever reads "يُنْزِفون" is saying: their wine will not run out. The Arabs say of people when their provisions have run out: «قد أنْزَفُوا» (they have run dry), «أقتروا», «أنفضوا», «أرمَلوا» and «أملقوا».

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
The companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it in the genitive, and that is the proper Arabic construction, even though most readers are for the nominative. (The latter) were wary of making the wide-eyed houris be "carried round" (yuṭāf bihinna), so they put them in the nominative, as in your saying: «and they have wide-eyed houris», or «with them are wide-eyed houris». The genitive is on the basis that you make the end of the statement follow its beginning, even if what is good in its beginning is not good in its end. One of the Arabs recited to me:
إذا ما الغانيات بَرَزْنَ يَوْماً * وزَجّجن الحواجب والعيونا
(When the fair women come out one day, having pencilled their eyebrows and eyes.)
The eye is not pencilled (with zajj); it is only lined with kohl; but he conjoined it to the eyebrows because the meaning is understood. Another recited to me:
ولقيتُ زوجك فى الوغى * متقلداً سيفاً ورمحاً
(I met your husband in battle, girded with a sword and a spear.)
A spear is not girded on; but he conjoined it to the sword. Another said:
تسمع للأحشاء منه لغطاً * ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدا
(You hear a clamour from his insides, and (see) stiffness and wide spread in his forelegs.)
One of Banū Dubayr recited to me:
علفتها تِبناً وماءً بارداً * حتى شَتَتْ همالةً عيناها
(I fed her straw and cool water, until she spent the winter with her eyes streaming.)
Water is not fed as fodder; it is only drunk; but he made it follow «التبن». Whoever read «وحورٌ عين» because — so he claimed — they are not carried round, ought to have said "وفاكهةٌ ولَحْم طير" as well, because fruit and meat are not carried round either; only wine is carried round. So there is a clear indication in that, for the genitive is the proper construction of the speech. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is «وحورا عيناً», intending the verb that you find (implied) in speech like this, as in the poet's saying:
جئنى بمثل بنى بَدْرٍ لقومهم * أو مثلَ أسرة منظور بن سيار
(Bring me the like of the Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār.)

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ قِيلاً سَلاَماً سَلاَماً﴾.
If you wish, you make «السلام» follow «القيل» (as badal), it being the same thing; and if you wish, you mean «إلاّ قيلَ سلامٍ سلامٍ». When you give it nunation, you put it in the accusative because the verb falls upon it. Had it been nominative — «قيلا سلامٌ سلامٌ» — it would have been permissible.
One of the Arabs, al-ʿUqaylī, recited to me:
فقلنا السلام فاتقت من أميرها * فَما كان إلا ومؤها بالحواجب
(We said "Peace!", and she was wary of her guardian, so there was nothing but her signalling with her eyebrows.)
He meant to quote the one who begins with the greeting. Al-Kisāʾī heard the Arabs say: «التقينا فقلنا: سلام سلام، ثم تفرقنا» (we met and said "Peace, peace", then we parted); he meant: we said "Peace be upon you", and they returned it to us.
«[Translator's note: «العقبلى» in the source is evidently a misprint for «العقيلى»; rendered as al-ʿUqaylī.]»

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي سِدْرٍ مَّخْضُودٍ﴾.
With no thorns in it.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَطَلْحٍ مَّنضُودٍ﴾.
Al-Kalbī mentioned that it is the banana; and it is said: it is the ṭalḥ (acacia) that you know.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَّمْدُودٍ﴾.
With no sun in it, like the shade between the break [191/ب] of dawn and sunrise.

farraa:32-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ لاَّ مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلاَ مَمْنُوعَةٍ﴾.
It does not come at one time and cease at another; it is always constant; «ولا ممنوعة»: (nor withheld) as the owners of orchards withhold their fruits.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفُرُشٍ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ﴾.
Some above others.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنشَأْنَاهُنَّ إِنشَآءً﴾.
He is saying: We re-created the young girl and the old woman and made them of equal age, thirty-three years old.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿عُرُباً﴾.
Its singular is «عَروب»: the woman who shows her love to her husband, the coquettish.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder told me, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I used to hear them read "عُرْباً أتراباً" with the light form (sukūn). It is like your saying «الرسْل» and «الكتْب» in the dialect of Tamīm and Bakr, with the light form; but the heavy form (with ḍamma) is the proper reading, because every «فعول», «فعيل» or «فِعال» that is pluralised on this pattern is heavy, whether masculine or feminine, and the readers follow that.
«[Translator's note: «ولتثقيل» is as printed, evidently for «والتثقيل».]»

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿لاًّصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
That is: this is for the companions of the right.

farraa:39-40.t:
His saying here: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ وَثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾.
He had said at the beginning of the sura: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِن الأوَّلين (13) وقليلٌ مِن الآخِرين﴾ (14). They mentioned that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wept, and it was hard on them,
(namely) His saying ﴿وقليل من الآخرين﴾. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed this: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ، وَثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾. It is nominative as a new sentence (istiʾnāf); or, if you wish, you make it nominative (as a predicate), saying: and the companions of the right have two throngs: a throng of these and a throng of those. The meaning is: they are two groups, a group of these and a group of those.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ﴾.
«اليحموم» is black smoke.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ بَارِدٍ وَلاَ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
The proper construction is for it to be genitive, following what precedes it; similar to it are ﴿زَيْتُونَةٍ لا شرقيةٍ وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾, and likewise ﴿وفاكهةٍ كثيرةٍ لا مقطُوعةٍ ولا ممنوعةٍ﴾. Had you made what follows nominative, it would have been correct Arabic speech. One of them recited to me:
وتُريكَ وجهاً كالصحيفةِ، لا * ظمآنُ مختلجٌ، ولا جَهْمُ
كعقيلةِ الدُّرِّ استضاءَ بها * محراب عرْش عزيزها العُجْمُ
(She shows you a face like a page, neither gaunt and twitching nor grim; like the choicest pearl, by which the non-Arabs lit up the sanctuary of their mighty one's throne.)
Another said:
ولقد أبِيت من الفتاة بمنزلٍ * فأبيت لا زانٍ ولا محروم
(I have spent the night in a place near the girl, and passed it neither an adulterer nor deprived.)
They begin anew with «لا»; but when they drop it, there is nothing for it but to make the end of the statement follow its beginning. The Arabs make «الكريم» follow anything from which they have negated a quality, intending blame by it. It is said: «أسمينٌ هذا؟» (Is this fat?), and you say: «ما هو بسمين ولا كريم» (it is neither fat nor fine); and «ما هذه الدار بواسعة ولا كريمة» (this house is neither spacious nor fine).

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ مُتْرَفِينَ﴾.
Living in luxury in this world.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَانُواْ يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى ٱلْحِنثِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
Associating partners with Allah (shirk): that is the great sin.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿لآكِلُونَ مِن شَجَرٍ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: «الآكلون من شجرة من زقوم». The meaning of «شجر» and «شجرة» is one, because when you say «أخذت من الشاء» (I took of the sheep), it is permissible whether you intend one or more than that.
«[Translator's note: «الآكلون» is as printed; presumably «لآكلون» is intended.]»

farraa:53-53.t:
Then He said: ﴿فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا﴾.
From the tree. Had He said «فمالئون منه», since He did not mention «الشجرة» (in the singular), it would have been correct, taking «منه» to refer to «الشجر». And «الشجر» is made feminine, so «منها» is a pronoun referring to «الشجر»; «الشجر» is treated as feminine and masculine, like «الثمر».

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْحَمِيمِ﴾.
If you wish, it refers to «الشجر»; and if you wish, to the eating.

farraa:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ ٱلْهِيمِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Kisāʾī told me, from a man of Banū Umayya called Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī, who said: I heard Ibn Jurayj read: "فشاربونَ شَرْب الهيم" with a fatḥa. He said: I mentioned that to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and he said: Is it not so? Has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Budayl ibn Warqāʾ al-Khuzāʿī to the people at Minā and said: "These are days of eating, drinking (shurb) and biʿāl."
Al-Farrāʾ said: «البِعال» means sexual intercourse. The rest of the readers give the shīn a ḍamma: "فشاربونَ شُرْب الهِيم". «الهيم» are camels struck by a disease so that they cannot quench their thirst with water; the singular is «أهيم» and the feminine «هيماء».
Some of the Arabs say «هائم», feminine «هائمة», then they pluralise it as «هيم», just as they said «عائط» and «عيط» (barren she-camels), and «حائل» and «حُول»; in meaning it is like «حائل / حُوْل», except that the ḍamma was dropped in «هيم» so that the yāʾ would not become a wāw. It is also said that «الهيم» is sand: He is saying that the people of the Fire will drink as soft sand (al-sihla) drinks. He said: al-Farrāʾ said: «الرملة» is itself «السهلة»; it is «سهلة» and «سِهلة».
«[Translator's note: the distinction between «سهلة» and «سهلة» at the end is lost in the unvowelled print (presumably «سَهْلة» and «سِهْلة»).]»

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّا تُمْنُونََ﴾.
He means: the drops of semen when they are cast into the wombs of women.
«[Translator's note: «قدفت» is as printed, evidently for «قذفت» (cast).]»

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿أأنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ﴾.
Do you create those drops, or are We the Creators? It is said of a man «مَنى» and «أمنى» (he emitted semen), and «مَذى» and «أمذى» (he emitted pre-seminal fluid); «أمنى» is more frequent than «منى», and «مذى» more frequent than «أمذى».
«[Translator's note: «أكثى» is as printed, evidently for «أكثر» (more frequent).]»

farraa:63-64.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ.﴾.
That is: (do you) make it grow?

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾.
You would wonder at what has befallen you in your crops. And it is said: the meaning of «تفكهون» is: you would regret.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾.
It is said: we are surely punished; and it is said: we are surely beset (by misfortune), and that is from their side.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً﴾.
It is salty, bitter water of extreme bitterness.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعاً لِّلْمُقْوِينَ﴾.
He means: a benefit for travellers when they halt in the «قِىّ» land, meaning the empty wilderness.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Abū Laylā al-Sijistānī told me, from Abū Jarīr, the judge of Sijistān, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: "فلا أُقْسِمَ بموقعِ النُّجومِ", and all the readers are for «مواقع».
Al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, tracing it back to ʿAbd Allāh as far as I know — al-Farrāʾ was unsure — [192/ب] he said: «فلا أقسم بموقع النجوم»; he said: by the muḥkam (firmly established) part of the Quran; and it used to come down to the Prophet ﷺ in instalments (nujūm).

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾: this shows that it is the Quran.
And it is said: «فلا أقسم بموقع النجوم» means by the setting-places of the stars when they set.

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَمَسُّهُ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: none touches that Preserved Tablet except the purified; he is saying: the angels, who have been purified of shirk. And it is said: «لا يمسه» means: none finds its taste and benefit except the purified, those who believe in it.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿أَنتُمْ مُّدْهِنُونَ﴾: deniers and disbelievers; I have heard both.

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.
It has come in the report: «تجعلون رزقكم» means: your thanks. In Arabic it is good to say: «جعلت زيارتى إياك أنك استخففت بى» (you made (the return for) my visiting you that you slighted me); the meaning then is: you made the reward of the visit to be rudeness. Likewise, you have made (your) thanks for provision to be denial.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلْحُلْقُومَ﴾. He means: the soul at death.

farraa:84-84.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ﴾. He means: the family of the dying person who are with him,
looking at him. The Arabs address a group with an action as though they all did it, while only some of them are meant, whether absent or present; this is of that kind, like your saying to a group: «أنتم قتلتم فلاناً» (you killed so-and-so), when only one absent person killed him. Do you not see that you might say to the people in a mosque, if they had harmed a man by crowding: «Fear Allah, for you are harming the Muslims», and it would be correct?
In much of speech you admonish someone other than the doer. It is asked: where is the answer (jawāb) of the first «فلولا» and the answer of the one after it? The answer to that is that both were answered with one answer, which is «ترجعونها»; and the Arabs sometimes repeat two particles whose meaning is one. This is of that kind; and of it is: ﴿فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنّكُمْ مِنِّى هُدًى فَمن تَبِعَ هُداىَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِم﴾: they were answered with one answer, though they are two conditional clauses (jazāʾān). And of that is His saying: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَّيُحِبُّون أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُم﴾,
and His saying: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إذا مِتُّم وكُنتُم تُراباً وعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُون﴾; and it has been explained in another place than this.
«[Translator's note: «أنت قتلتم» is as printed, evidently for «أنتم قتلتم»; translated accordingly. «الموضوع» at the end is likewise as printed, for «الموضع» (place).]»

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾: (not) owned; and I have heard: (not) requited.
«[Translator's note: «مجزبين» is as printed, evidently for «مجزيين» (requited).]»

farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾: of the people of the Garden of ʿAdn.

farraa:89-89.t:
﴿فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: an elder told me, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "فَروح وريحان"; and al-Ḥasan's reading is likewise. Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, the people of Medina and the rest of the readers (read) (فرَوحٌ), that is: rest in the grave. Whoever reads (فرُوحٌ) is saying: a life in which there is no death; and (وريحان): sustenance.
«[Translator's note: the vowelling of the reading attributed to ʿĀʾisha and al-Ḥasan is printed «فَروح», but the contrast drawn requires «فرُوح» (with ḍamma), which is how it is transmitted from them.]»

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَلاَمٌ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
That is: that is granted to you, that you are of the companions of the right. «أنّ» was dropped while its meaning remains, as you say «أنت مصدّق مسافر عن قليل» (you are believed, travelling shortly) when he had said: «I am travelling shortly».
Likewise you find its meaning to be: you are believed that you are travelling; and its meaning (here) is: peace to you, you being of the companions of the right. It may also be like a prayer for him, as in your saying: «فسقيا لك من الرجال» (may you be watered, of all men!). If you make «السلام» nominative, it is a prayer.
And Allah knows best what is correct.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "such-and-such will take place".

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «لوقعتها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «ليس», whose noun (ism) is «كاذبة», and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الواقعة».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «خافضة»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it", and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a second ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الْوَاقِعَةُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إذا» is a badal (substitute) from the earlier «إذا» and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what that is attached to.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «فكانت» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «بُسَّتْ»; «منبثَّا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «هباء».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and the interrogative clause «ما أصحاب», made up of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), is the khabar of «أصحاب».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: (وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause of the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding clause.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «والسابقون»: the wāw is conjunctive; «السابقون» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the second «السابقون» is a tawkīd (emphasis).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «أولئك المقربون» is the khabar (predicate) of {السَّابِقُونَ}, and the clause of the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause in verse (8).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition «في جنات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {الْمُقَرَّبُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «ثلة» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are a throng", and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الْمُقَرَّبُونَ}; the preposition «من الأولين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ثلة».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «وقليل»: a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ثلة», and the preposition «من الآخرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «قليل».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The preposition «على سرر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هم», i.e. "they are a throng upon couches".

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (متكئين عليها متقابلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «على سرر», i.e. "they being upon couches, reclining"; the preposition «عليها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «يطوف» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in {مُتَقَابِلِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition «بأكواب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَطُوفُ}; the preposition «من معين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كأس».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «لا يُصَدَّعون» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «كأس».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: His words «وفاكهة»: a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «أكواب»; the preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فاكهة».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «لحم».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «حور» is mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted by its being qualified; the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "they have".

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «كأمثال» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective) of «حور».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «جزاء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (جزاء).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «قيلا» is excepted with a disconnected exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ); «سلاما» is a badal (substitute), and the second «سلاما» is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) (tawkīd lafẓī).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The wāw is resumptive; «أصحاب» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «ما أصحاب اليمين» is the khabar (predicate) of «أصحاب».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «في سدر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate) of the first «أصحاب».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «لا مقطوعة»: «لا» is negative, and «مقطوعة» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «فاكهة»; the second «لا» is redundant (zāʾida); «ممنوعة» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «مقطوعة».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: (لأصحاب اليمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلناهن».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «ثلة»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they".

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition «من الآخرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ثلة».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «أصحاب» is mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is the clause «ما أصحاب الشمال», and the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause in verse (27).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: (في سموم وحميم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) {أَصْحَابُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «لا بارد»: «لا» is negative; «بارد» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يحموم».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: (إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك مترفين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the adverb «قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مترفين».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: «إذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e. "we will be raised", and the clause «إنا لمبعوثون» explains the implied verb.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The wāw is conjunctive; «آباؤنا» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "will be raised"; the clause (آباؤنا مبعوثون) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «إنا لمبعوثون».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The preposition «إلى ميقات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مجموعون».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «ثم إنكم لآكلون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying), and the vocative clause is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «لآكلون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; the preposition «من شجر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آكلون»; the preposition «مِنْ زَقُّوم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شجر».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «فمالئون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «آكلون»; the preposition «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مالئون»; «البطون» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مالئون».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: «فشاربون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «مالئون», and the two prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شاربون».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نزلهم», and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «فلولا تُصًدَّقون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «نحن خلقناكم»; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ).

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «أفرأيتم» is resumptive; its two objects are «ما» and the clause {أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) one. As for a clause occurring after it, they answered that the khabar (predicate) coming after «نحن» was brought by way of emphasis; supporting its being connected is that the statement calls for "which of the two matters is the case?", so what follows it is a clause interpreted as a single word.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «نحن قَدَّرْنا» is resumptive, and the clause «ما نحن بمسبوقين» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive (majrūr) and attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مسبوقين».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The wāw is resumptive; the clause «فلولا تذكَّرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «علمتم»; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ).

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The clause «أفرأيتم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to its counterpart in verse (58), and the two objects of the verb are «ما» and the following interrogative clause.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: (أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] See the i'rab of verse (59).

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «فظلتم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لجعلناه»; «ظلتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb from which one of its two lāms was dropped for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «إنا لمغرمون» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an omitted saying, and the clause of the omitted saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in {تَفَكَّهُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: (بل نحن محرومون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «أفرأيتم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to its counterpart in verse (63), and its two objects are «الماء» and the following interrogative clause.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: (أأنتم أنزلتموه من المزن أم نحن المنزلون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] See the i'rab of verse (59).

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «فلولا تشكرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «جعلناه»; «لولا» is for urging (taḥḍīḍ).

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «أفرأيتم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to its counterpart in verse (68), and its two objects are «النار» and the interrogative clause.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The clause «نحن جعلناها» is resumptive; «تذكرة» is the second object; the preposition «للمقوين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «متاعا».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «فسبح باسم ربك» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «فلا أقسم» is resumptive; «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: The wāw is parenthetical, and the clause (وإنه لقسم عظيم) is parenthetical between «أقسم» and its response; the clause «لو تعلمون» is parenthetical between the adjective and the noun it qualifies, and the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being "you would have believed".

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: (إنه لقرآن كريم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause of the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The preposition «في كتاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second naʿt (adjective) of «قرآن».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: The clause «لا يمسُّه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قرآن».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: «تنزيل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قرآن»; the preposition «من رب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «تنزيل».

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; the preposition «بهذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مدهنون», and the clause «أنتم مدهنون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The clause «وتجعلون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the single-word khabar (predicate) {مُدْهِنُونَ}, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) that governs the later verb «ترجعونها»; his words «فلولا ترجعونها» refer to the soul. «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the later verb «ترجعونها».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: (وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «حين» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «تنظرون».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: (ونحن أقرب إليه منكم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "you look on in this state"; the two prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقرب», and the clause «ولكن لا تُبصرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تنظرون».

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: «فلولا» is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of its counterpart in verse (83). The conditional clause «إن كنتم» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by {تَرْجِعُونَهَا}; its place is originally earlier, i.e. "if you are not to be judged, then bring back the departing soul".

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: The clause «ترجعونها» is resumptive; its place is originally after the first «لولا». The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are truthful, then bring back the soul".

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: (فأما إن كان من المقربين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive; «أمَّا» is a particle of condition and detailing.

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: His words «فروح»: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and «روح» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then his recompense is rest"; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «أمَّا», and the apodosis of «إن» is omitted, indicated by the apodosis [of «أمَّا»].

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «وأما إن كان ... » is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «إن كان من المقربين».

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and «سلام» is mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إمَّا» [Translator's note: so written in the source; «أمَّا» is meant], and the apodosis of «إنْ» is omitted, indicated by the apodosis of «إمَّا». The preposition «من أصحاب» is attached to the implied notion of being (istiqrār) to which «لك» is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); «نزل» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then his recompense is a hospitality"; the preposition «من حميم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نزل».

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: The clause «لهو حق» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, إِذا وَقعت الْوَاقِعَة: إذا is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), and the governing word in it is وقعت, because it is sometimes used as a conditional, so the verb after it governs it, just as [the verb] governs the conditional ما and من in your saying ما تفعل أفعل ("whatever you do, I will do") and من تكرم أكرم ("whomever you honour, I will honour"); من and ما are in the position of the accusative by the verb after them, without disagreement. If the interrogative alif enters upon إذا, it leaves the domain of the condition, so the verb after it does not govern it, because it is annexed to what follows it, as in أئذا متنا, أئذا كنا and the like. Al-Naḥḥās permitted متنا to govern إذا, and that is far-fetched.
إذا was not used as a conditional in all speech and made to govern [the jussive] like the others only because it differs from the conditional particles, owing to the definiteness and timing it carries regarding the occurrence of what follows it and its being without uncertainty, whereas the other conditional particles are only for a thing that may occur and may not occur. إذا may be used for a thing that must necessarily occur, as in إذا السماء انشقت and إذا الشمس كورت and the like.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying خافضة رَافِعَة: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is abasing, exalting" (هي خافضة رافعة), a khabar (predicate) after a khabar. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الواقعة, and there is remoteness in it, because the ḥāl in most of its cases is only for what may be and may not be, while there is no doubt about the Resurrection that it raises some people to the Garden and lowers others to the Fire; that is inevitable, so there is no benefit in the ḥāl. Al-Farrāʾ permitted it on the assumption of an implied وقعت: "it occurred abasing, exalting" (وقعت خافضة رافعة).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying إِذا رجت: the governing word in إذا according to al-Zajjāj is وقعت. This is far-fetched if you make وقعت govern the first إذا; if you imply another governing word for the first إذا, it is good for وقعت to govern the second إذا — unless you make the second إذا a badal (substitute) of the first, in which case it is permissible for وقعت to govern both of them together.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying فأصحاب الميمنة مَا أَصْحَاب الميمنة: the first أصحاب is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ما is a second mubtadaʾ; it is an interrogative whose meaning is wonder and magnification. The second أصحاب is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and ما with its khabar is the khabar of the first أصحاب. That is permissible although there is nothing in the clause referring back to the mubtadaʾ, because the meaning is "what are they?" (ما هم), and هم refers back to the first mubtadaʾ; so it is speech construed according to its meaning, not its wording. Like it are الحاقة ما الحاقة and القارعة ما القارعة. The second noun was only made overt — while its right was to be a pronoun, since it had already been made overt — so that it would be grander in magnification and wonder, and more eloquent. Also like it is وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His saying وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ: the first is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second its naʿt (adjective), and أولئك المقربون is a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of the first. It is also said that the first السابقون is a mubtadaʾ and the second its khabar, and أولئك is a second khabar or a badal (substitute), in the sense "those foremost in obedience to Allah are those foremost to the mercy of Allah".
His saying ثلة: the khabar of a mubtadaʾ [omitted], i.e. "they are a multitude" (هم ثلة); وقليل is conjoined to it, and على سرر is a second khabar.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying متكئين and متقابلين: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in سرر. Had على سرر been non-functioning (mulghā), not a khabar (predicate), there would be no pronoun in it.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying وحور عين: whoever reads it in the nominative construes it according to the meaning, because the meaning of the speech is "in it are cups and jugs" (فيها أكواب وأباريق), so وحور عين is conjoined according to the meaning and not conjoined according to the wording. Whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to what precedes it and also construes it according to the meaning, because the meaning is "they enjoy fruit and meat and maidens with wide eyes". The accusative is permissible, also construing it according to the meaning, because the meaning of "there circulate among them such-and-such" is "they are given such-and-such"; then حورا is conjoined to its meaning.
His saying عين: it is the plural of عيناء, and its origin is عُيْن on the pattern فُعْل, as you say حمراء and حُمْر. The عين [the first letter] was given a kasra so that the yāʾ would not change into a wāw and so resemble the words with wāw [as a radical]; there is not in the speech of the Arabs a quiescent yāʾ preceded by a ḍamma nor a quiescent wāw preceded by a kasra. Some Arabs say حِير عِين, by assimilation of vowels (itbāʿ).
His saying جَزَاء: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it is also said: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying إِلَّا قيلا: accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); it is also said: accusative by يسمعون.
His saying سَلاما سَلاما: accusative by the saying [as its object]; it is also said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of قيل. In ordinary speech the nominative is permissible, in the sense of سلام عليكم ("peace be upon you"), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying إِنَّا أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ: the pronoun refers back to الحور mentioned earlier. Al-Akhfash said it is a pronoun for which no mention has preceded, except that its meaning is known. [Translator's note: the edition prints «ضنير» for ضمير.]

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying عربا: it is the plural of عَروب; whoever makes the رآء quiescent does so by lightening, as in عَضُد and عَضْد. And الأتراب is the plural of تِرْب.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying أئذا متْنا: whoever gives the ميم of متنا a kasra makes its verb come on the pattern فَعِل يَفْعَل, like خاف يخاف, and the imperfect according to him is يَمات. It is also said that it is anomalous among the weak verbs, coming on the pattern فَعِل يَفْعُل with a ḍamma on the second radical in the imperfect, just as there came among the sound verbs فَضِل يَفْضُل on the pattern فَعِل يَفْعُل, and that too is anomalous.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying شرب الهيم: whoever gives the شين a fatḥa makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of شرب; whoever gives it a ḍamma makes it a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar). Its accusative is as a maṣdar, i.e. "a drinking like the drinking of thirsty camels" (شربا مثل شرب الهيم); then the thing described and the muḍāf were omitted, and parallels of this have preceded. الهيم is the plural of هيماء, and the هاء was given a kasra so that the yāʾ would not change into a wāw; so it is like عين. It is also said that it is the plural of هائم.

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His saying فظلتم: its origin is ظللتم, then the first lām was omitted. It has been read with a kasra on the ظاء [فظِلتم], on the basis that the vowel of the first lām was transferred onto the ظاء, and then [the lām] was omitted.

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying لَا يمسهُ إِلَّا الْمُطهرُونَ: this ḍamma in يمسه may be a case ending (iʿrāb), with لا negating, i.e. "none touches it except the purified", meaning the angels; so it is a statement and not a prohibition. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda and others. It is also said that لا is for prohibition and the ḍamma in يمسه is an indeclinable vowel (bināʾ), the verb being jussive; so it is a command from Allah that none but a pure person should touch the Qur'an. This is the doctrine of Mālik and others. So the meaning of purification on the first view is [purity] from sins and transgressions, and on the second view purification with water.

mekki-muskil:88-88.t:
His saying فَأَما إِن كَانَ: the apodosis of أما and of إنْ is in the فاء in His saying فروح, i.e. "then for him is rest" (فله روح), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is also said that the فاء is the apodosis of أما, and إنْ has its apodosis in what precedes it, because it did not govern [anything] in the wording. Al-Mubarrad said: the apodosis of إنْ is omitted.
Nothing follows أما but nouns and clauses, yet it contains the sense of a condition, and its right was that nothing should follow it but a verb, because of the condition in it. But it stands in for a verb, because its meaning is "whatever the case may be, the matter is such-and-such" (مهما يكن من شيء فالأمر كذا وكذا). Since it stands by itself in place of a verb, and a verb is not followed by a verb, it became impossible for a verb to follow it, and a noun or clauses follow it. The noun is to be assumed as coming after its apodosis. So if you want to know the case of the noun after it, put مهما in its place, assume the noun after the فاء, and bring the فاء onto the verb. The meaning of أما according to Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] is that it is a departure from one thing to another, i.e. "leave what we were on and take up something else".

mekki-muskil:91-91.t:
His saying فسلام لَك: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
His saying فَنزل: i.e. "then for them is a hospitality" (فلهم نزل), and من حميم is a naʿt (adjective) of نزل; it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar.

mekki-muskil:95-95.t: His saying حق الْيَقِين: اليقين is an adjective that has taken the place of the thing described; its implied form is "the truth of the certain report" (حق الخبر اليقين).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إذا وقعت الواقعة﴾: «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time containing the meaning of a condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its implied (muqaddar) apodosis; there are other possibilities in its i'rab. «وقعت» is a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; «الواقعة» is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma; the clause is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: «خفضت أقوامًا ورفعت آخرين» (it lowered some peoples and raised others); and the conditional clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ليس لوقعتها كاذبة﴾: «ليس» is an inert (jāmid), defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; «لوقعتها» is its fronted khabar (predicate), and the lām is in the sense of «في» (in), on the assumption of an implied muḍāf; «كاذبة» is the noun of «ليس». «كاذبة» is a ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. «نفس كاذبة» (a lying soul); and it has been said: «كاذبة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has come in the form of an active participle, meaning «الكذب» (lying).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿خافضة رافعة﴾: «خافضة» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and «رافعة» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إذا رجت الأرض رجا﴾: «إذا» is a badal (substitute) of the first «إذا», or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it, or its khabar (predicate) on the view that it [the first «إذا»] is a mubtadaʾ (subject), or it is conditional; the governing word in it is either implied (muqaddar) or the verb that follows it. «رجت» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; «الأرض» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ); «رجًّا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb); and the clause «رجت» is in the position of a genitive.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وبست الجبال بسا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «بست» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; «الجبال» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ); «بسًّا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb); and the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فكانت هباء منبثا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «كانت» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هي» (it); «هباء» is its khabar (predicate), and «منبثًّا» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «هباء».

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وكنتم أزواجا ثلاثة﴾: conjoined to «رجت»; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, «أزواجًا» is its khabar (predicate), and «ثلاثة» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجًا».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فأصحاب الميمنة ما أصحاب الميمنة﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), to begin detailing and explaining the states of the three kinds; «أصحاب الميمنة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is interrogative, in the position of a nominative as a second mubtadaʾ; the second «أصحاب الميمنة» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; and the clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. Repeating the mubtadaʾ here in its own wording makes the linking element (rābiṭ), namely the pronoun, unnecessary.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة﴾: conjoined to what precedes.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿والسابقون السابقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «السابقون» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and [the second] «السابقون» is a tawkīd (emphasis).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أولئك المقربون﴾: «أولئك» is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); «المقربون» is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw, or a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; the clause is the khabar of «السابقون», and the demonstrative makes the linking element (rābiṭ), namely the pronoun, unnecessary.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿في جنات النعيم﴾: a second khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «المقربون», or attached to (mutaʿalliq) it.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿ثلة من الأولين﴾: «ثلة» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هم ثلة من الأولين» (they are a large company of the former peoples), and «من الأولين» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وقليل من الآخرين﴾: «قليل» is conjoined to «ثلة», and «من الآخرين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قليل». And it has been said: «ثلة» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) because it is qualified, and the khabar (predicate) is «على سرر» which comes next.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿على سرر موضونة﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هم»; «موضونة» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سرر», genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿متكئين عليها متقابلين﴾: «متكئين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in the khabar «على سرر», accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a masculine plural; «عليها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; and «متقابلين» is a second ḥāl, accusative.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿يطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطوف»; «ولدان» is the fāʿil (agent), and «مخلدون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ولدان».

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿بأكواب وأباريق وكأس من معين﴾: «بأكواب» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطوف», and what comes after it is conjoined to it; «من معين» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «الكأس».

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿لا يصدعون عنها ولا ينزفون﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم». «لا» is negative; «يصدعون» is built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «عنها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; and «لا ينزفون» is conjoined to «لا يصدعون».

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وفاكهة مما يتخيرون﴾: conjoined to what precedes; «مما» is a naʿt (adjective) of «فاكهة», and the clause «يتخيرون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿ولحم طير مما يشتهون﴾: «لحم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «فاكهة», genitive (majrūr), and «طير» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «لحم»; «ما» is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a genitive; «يشتهون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وحور عين﴾: it is read in the nominative, and there are several views on it. The first: it is conjoined to «ولدان». The second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. «لهم حور» (they have ḥūr). The third: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «ونساؤهم حور» (and their women are ḥūr). It is read in the accusative on the implied form «يعطون، أو يجازون حورًا» (they are given, or rewarded with, ḥūr). And it is read in the genitive, conjoined to «أكواب» in wording but not in meaning, because the ḥūr are not carried round [to them]; and it has been said: it is conjoined to «جنات», i.e. «في جنات وفي حور» (in gardens and among ḥūr). «عين» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «حور».

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون﴾: in «كأمثال» the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as a second naʿt (adjective) of «حور»; «أمثال» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), «اللؤلؤ» is muḍāf ilayhi, and «المكنون» is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿جزاء بما كانوا يعملون﴾: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of reward, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. «يجزون جزاء» (they are rewarded with a reward). «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جزاء»; the clause «كانوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause «يعملون» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا تأثيما﴾: «لا» is negative; «يسمعون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسمعون»; «لغوًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction, «لا» is negative, and «تأثيمًا» is conjoined to «لغوًا».

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿إلا قيلا سلاما سلاما﴾: «إلا» is a particle of exception, and the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ); «قيلًا» is a disjoined excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), necessarily accusative. As for «سلامًا سلامًا», there are several views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) of «قيلًا», i.e. they hear nothing in it except «سلامًا سلامًا». The second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «قيلًا». The third: it is made accusative by «قيلًا», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. except that they say «سلامًا سلامًا». The fourth: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. «سلموا سلامًا» (they gave greetings of peace).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وأصحاب اليمين ما أصحاب اليمين﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «أصحاب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; «أصحاب اليمين» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; and the clause is the khabar of «أصحاب».

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿في سدر مخضود﴾: a second khabar (predicate) of «أصحاب», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هم في سدر» (they are among lote-trees); «مخضود» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سدر».

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿وطلح منضود﴾: a second khabar (predicate) of «أصحاب», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هم في سدر», and «مخضود» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سدر». [Translator's note: this text repeats the comment on the previous ayah (56:28) word for word and does not treat «طلح» or «منضود»; presumably «طلح» is conjoined to «سدر» and «منضود» is a naʿt of «طلح», as with the following ayahs.]

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وظل ممدود﴾: conjoined to His saying «في سدر», and «ممدود» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿وماء مسكوب﴾: conjoined to His saying «في سدر», and «مسكوب» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وفاكهة كثيرة﴾: conjoined to His saying «في سدر», and «كثيرة» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿لا مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة﴾: conjoined to His saying «في سدر», and the «لا» in «لا مقطوعة» is for negation. [Translator's note: «لا مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة» qualifies «فاكهة» in the preceding ayah; the source's «conjoined to في سدر» is translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وفرش مرفوعة﴾: conjoined to His saying «في سدر», and «مرفوعة» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿إنا أنشأناهن إنشاء﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «نا» is its noun, the clause «أنشأناهن» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and «إنشاء» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فجعلناهن أبكارا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «جعلناهن» is a past verb, a fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «أبكارًا» is a second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿لأصحاب اليمين﴾: «لأصحاب اليمين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنشأناهن».

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿ثلة من الأولين﴾: «ثلة» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من الأولين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ثلة».

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿وثلة من الآخرين﴾: «ثلة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first «ثلة», nominative (marfūʿ); «من الآخرين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «ثلة».

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿وأصحاب الشمال ما أصحاب الشمال﴾: «أصحاب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; «أصحاب الشمال» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the clause is the khabar of «أصحاب»; and the speech is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿في سموم وحميم﴾: a second khabar (predicate), or the khabar of an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿وظل من يحموم﴾: «ظل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «سموم», genitive (majrūr); «من يحموم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «ظل».

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿لا بارد ولا كريم﴾: conjoined to what precedes, and the «لا» in «لا بارد» is for negation.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك مترفين﴾: the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «هم» is its noun, and the clause «كانوا» is its khabar (predicate); «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw of the plural is its noun; the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or to «مترفين»; and «مترفين» is the khabar of «كان».

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وكانوا يصرون على الحنث العظيم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause «يصرون» is its khabar (predicate); «على الحنث» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصرون»; and «العظيم» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وكانوا يقولون أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أئنا لمبعوثون﴾: also conjoined. «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause «يقولون» is its khabar (predicate). The hamza is for interrogation; «إذا» is a conditional adverb (ẓarf), attached to (mutaʿalliq) something indicated by His saying «أئنا لمبعوثون»; «متنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «كنا» is conjoined to «متنا»; «كان» is a defective past verb, «نا» is its noun, «ترابًا» is its khabar, and «عظامًا» is conjoined to «ترابًا». The hamza is for interrogation; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «نا» is its noun, [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «مبعوثون» is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿أوآباؤنا الأولون﴾: the hamza is for interrogation and the wāw is a conjunction; «آباؤنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun latent in «مبعوثون». Conjoining to the pronoun without the emphasis «نحن» is acceptable because of the separating element, namely the hamza. And it has been said: what it is conjoined to is the position of «إن» and its noun, after taking into account that the conjoined word has been placed before the khabar (predicate), the implied form being: «أئنا أو آباؤنا مبعوثون» (shall we, or our fathers, be raised?). «الأولون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آباؤنا».

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿قل إن الأولين والآخرين﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «قل» is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (you); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «الأولين» is its noun, «الآخرين» is conjoined to «الأولين», and «الآخرين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأولين». [Translator's note: the source states the last point twice; both are translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿لمجموعون إلى ميقات يوم معلوم﴾: [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «مجموعون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «إن» with its noun and khabar is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying); «إلى ميقات يوم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مجموعون»; and «معلوم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوم».

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿ثم إنكم أيها الضالون المكذبون﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay, falling within the scope of the saying; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «كم» is its noun; «أي» is a vocative, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); «الضالون» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «أي», and «المكذبون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الضالون».

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿لآكلون من شجر من زقوم﴾: [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «آكلون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنكم»; «من شجر» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آكلون»; and «من زقوم» is a badal (substitute) of His saying «من شجر», or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿فمالئون منها البطون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «مالئون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «آكلون»; «منها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مالئون»; and «البطون» is the object of the active participle.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿فشاربون عليه من الحميم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «شاربون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «آكلون»; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and «من الحميم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «شاربون».

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿فشاربون شرب الهيم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «شاربون» is conjoined to what precedes; «شرب» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «الهيم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿هذا نزلهم يوم الدين﴾: «هذا» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «نزلهم» is the khabar (predicate), and «يوم الدين»: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿نحن خلقناكم فلولا تصدقون﴾: «نحن» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «خلقناكم» is the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); «تصدقون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿أفرأيتم ما تمنون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is a conjunction; «رأيتم» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي» (that which), the first object of «رأيتم»; and the clause «تمنون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position.
